metadata.file_name: 4. Zheng et al. (2023). Identifying key features of resilient students in digital reading: Insights from a machine learning approach.pdf
metadata.title: Identifying key features of resilient students in digital reading: Insights from a machine learning approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 microdata and constructs an analytic sample of ESCS-disadvantaged students who are classified as academically resilient (ARS) or non-academically resilient (NRS) based on reading performance. The manuscript describes data cleaning (removing invalid responses coded as 999), kNN imputation for missing/invalid responses, min–max normalization to [0,1], and class-imbalance handling via SMOTETomek, followed by an SVM model with class-weighting and SVM-RFE feature selection. No PISA sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are mentioned, and the analysis is implemented in Python (scikit-learn/imbalanced-learn), which typically does not natively incorporate complex survey weights. Therefore, the weighting strategy is treated as unweighted/unspecified for the ML pipeline, and the paper does not report any weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or design-based variance estimation.

data.outcome_summary: Using PISA 2018, the study classifies academically resilient students (ARS) vs non-academically resilient students (NRS) among 11,496 ESCS-disadvantaged 15-year-olds from seven Asian economies. A supervised SVM with linear kernel and SVM-RFE feature selection was trained on 105 contextual features and evaluated with 10-fold cross-validation. With all features, the model achieved an average accuracy of 87.51% and AUC of 94.86%, with recall 95.98%, precision 83.11%, and F-measure 88.63%. After selecting the optimal top-20 feature subset, performance remained high: average accuracy 84.35%, AUC 92.34%, recall 91.51%, precision 80.69%, and F-measure 85.42%. The most influential predictors included metacognitive strategies in digital reading (METASPAM, METASUM, UNDREM) and reading enjoyment (JOYREAD), while ICT-related features showed mixed/controversial effects (e.g., ICTRES and AUTICT vs SOIAICT).
